narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the purpose of the loan, and your credit history. Your checking account status of 0-200 DM was the single biggest reason for the denial. Most approved applicants (59%) have no checking account at all or maintain higher balances, so your relatively low balance pushed the prediction noticeably toward higher risk.

The fact that you are requesting the loan to purchase a used car worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. This purpose is viewed more favorably than many other loan reasons. Similarly, your past delays in credit history also helped your case by reducing the predicted risk, though this positive effect was not strong enough to overcome the concerns raised by your checking account.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that the risk was too high to approve the loan. To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a stronger checking account balance over the next several months before reapplying. This single change would likely have the largest positive impact on how a similar model evaluates your application.
